pr_title: collab: Make unsupported for MinGW toolchain
pr_body:
Closes #23451

reverts #23117 for MinGW. collab can't be compiled for MinGW because webrtc itself doesn't support MinGW compilers

Release Notes:

- N/A
pr_comments: confirming that it fixes an issue with msys2 (ran clippy)

Just leaving my two cents here that I'm not sure that this is worth it.

It adds a lot of noise to the code with all of the conditional compilation, and I don't think we've ever explicitly stated that supporting MinGW for our Windows builds.

Is there any particular reason we would _need_ to support MinGW over MSVC on Windows?

> Is there any particular reason we would _need_ to support MinGW over MSVC on Windows?

I don't see a problem if community will support this (https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/23451#issuecomment-2606461190)

> > Is there any particular reason we would _need_ to support MinGW over MSVC on Windows?
> 
> I don't see a problem if community will support this ([#23451 (comment)](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/23451#issuecomment-2606461190))

The problem is that it adds additional complexity to the codebase that Zed engineers have to deal with, for a platform toolchain that we don't use ourselves.

Additionally, I don't think that long-term we want to support a build of Zed that purposefully doesn't include core Zed features (like collaboration).

In the original issue (#23451) the problem was identified as:

> then cargo will build webrtc-sys, but webrtc itself supports MSVC only

So I think the path forward here would be to add support for building the crates/libraries required to support collaboration on MinGW.

EDIT: I wouldn't say I'm totally opposed to merging this PR as a temporary measure, but I feel strongly that the long-term fix to support MinGW is to fix the underlying issues of the required libraries not building there.

> EDIT: I wouldn't say I'm totally opposed to merging this PR as a temporary measure, but I feel strongly that the long-term fix to support MinGW is to fix the underlying issues of the required libraries not building there.
